name: Marvin Gaye
hook: The Motown singer who beat Berry Gordy's refusal to release a political album, and who later built his biggest hit on a TR-808 drum machine in Belgium.
blurb: Marvin Gaye was born in Washington, D.C., on 2 April 1939. He signed to Motown's Tamla label in 1960, played drums on other people's sessions, released his first solo single in 1961, and through the 1960s became one of the label's most reliable hitmakers, including 'I Heard It Through the Grapevine' with Norman Whitfield. In 1971 he made 'What's Going On', an album about war, racism, police violence and pollution. Motown's boss, Berry Gordy, said it was too political for the radio and would not release it. Gaye refused to record anything else until he did. The album became a huge hit, and after that Gaye was one of the first Motown artists to produce his own records. After leaving America to escape tax debts, he signed to Columbia in March 1982 and recorded 'Midnight Love' in Belgium and Germany. 'Sexual Healing', written in Ostend and released on 9 October 1982, was made on a drum machine, the Roland TR-808, which he chose because it let him make a record without other musicians or producers. On 1 April 1984, the day before his 45th birthday, he was shot and killed by his father at his parents' house in Los Angeles.
